question: What distinguishes complementary therapies from alternative therapies?

options.A: Complementary therapies are used alongside conventional medicine, while alternative therapies are used in place of it.
options.B: Alternative therapies are always scientifically proven, whereas complementary therapies are not.
options.C: Complementary therapies are only used in rural areas, while alternative therapies are used in hospitals.
options.D: There is no difference; the terms are completely interchangeable.

explanation: Complementary therapies are utilized in conjunction with standard Western medical treatments, whereas alternative therapies replace conventional medical approaches entirely. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h1)

question: Why is it important for Nigerian nurses to maintain a non-judgmental attitude toward CAM use?

options.A: So patients feel safe disclosing their CAM use without fear of judgment.
options.B: Because nurses are legally required to prescribe CAM products.
options.C: To ensure patients stop taking all conventional medications.
options.D: So the hospital can generate more revenue from herbal sales.

explanation: Patients often hide their use of CAM out of fear of disapproval, making a non-judgmental approach vital for open communication and accurate patient assessment. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h1)

question: What is the primary philosophy of integrative health in modern healthcare?

options.A: Treating only the physical symptoms of a specific disease.
options.B: Treating the whole person—mind, body, and spirit—by combining mainstream and evidence-based complementary practices.
options.C: Replacing all Western medicines with traditional herbal remedies.
options.D: Eliminating traditional practices from clinical settings entirely.

explanation: Integrative health focuses on holistic care that addresses the whole person by merging conventional treatments with evidence-based complementary therapies. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h2)

question: How does understanding the historical context of traditional healing help Nigerian nurses?

options.A: It helps them diagnose complex infectious diseases without laboratory tests.
options.B: It explains why patients hold specific health beliefs and fosters respectful, collaborative care.
options.C: It allows nurses to legally practice as traditional bone-setters.
options.D: It proves that Western medicine is completely ineffective.

explanation: Knowing the historical roots of traditional healing gives insight into patient beliefs, helping nurses build trust and respect for diverse healing traditions. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h2)

question: Which category of complementary therapy includes herbal medicines, vitamins, and dietary supplements?
explanation: Herbal remedies, vitamins, minerals, and dietary supplements fall under the classification of natural products. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h3)

question: Massage therapy and traditional bone-setting belong to which category of complementary therapies?
explanation: Manipulative and body-based practices focus on structures and systems of the body, including massage and traditional bone-setting. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h3)

question: Why is the assumption that 'natural' remedies are completely safe considered dangerous?

options.A: Natural products are always more expensive than prescription drugs.
options.B: Natural remedies contain active chemical constituents that can cause adverse side effects and drug interactions.
options.C: Natural products do not contain any chemical components.
options.D: Herbal supplements can only be prescribed by medical doctors.

explanation: Even though they are natural, herbal products contain active chemicals that can interact dangerously with prescription medications and cause side effects. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h4)

question: What is a primary nursing responsibility regarding CAM and patient safety?

options.A: Proactively screening patients for supplement use and educating them on potential herb-drug interactions.
options.B: Forbidding patients from ever using any local herbs.
options.C: Replacing all prescribed medications with herbal teas.
options.D: Prescribing standardized herbal dosages without a doctor's order.

explanation: Nurses must assess for supplement use and provide education regarding potential toxicities and interactions to protect patient safety. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h4)

question: What specific details should a nurse explore when assessing a patient's CAM use?

options.A: Only the financial cost of the herbal product.
options.B: The reason for use, duration, dosage, and any observed side effects or benefits.
options.C: The political affiliations of the herbalist who sold the product.
options.D: Whether the product is manufactured exclusively in Western countries.

explanation: A comprehensive nursing assessment covers why the therapy is used, how long, at what dose, and any effects experienced. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h5)

question: How do nurses act as bridges of communication in Nigerian clinical settings regarding CAM?

options.A: By helping patients navigate both orthodox hospitals and traditional practices safely through education.
options.B: By translating medical documents into local dialects only.
options.C: By performing traditional surgeries inside the hospital ward.
options.D: By preventing doctors from talking to patients about their diets.

explanation: Nurses bridge the gap by fostering open dialogue and educating patients who utilize both orthodox and traditional care systems. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h5)

question: Which regulatory body defines the legal scope of nursing practice in Nigeria?

options.B: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN)
options.D: The Federal Ministry of Indigenous Healing

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN) establishes the legal scope and standards for professional nursing practice in the country. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h6)

question: How do ethical principles of autonomy and beneficence apply to CAM use in nursing?

options.A: Autonomy gives patients the right to choose treatments, while beneficence obligates nurses to protect them from harm.
options.B: Autonomy means nurses decide everything, and beneficence means free medication for all.
options.C: Beneficence requires stopping all traditional practices, and autonomy forbids patient education.
options.D: They only apply to surgical operations and not to herbal remedies.

explanation: Patient autonomy respects their right to make healthcare choices, and beneficence ensures nurses act in ways that promote safety and well-being. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h6)

question: What is the primary foundation of Evidence-Based Practice in nursing when evaluating CAM?

options.A: Relying strictly on personal opinions and traditional folklore.
options.B: Integrating best research evidence with clinical expertise and patient values.
options.C: Following whatever treatment is most popular on social media.
options.D: Using only conventional Western medications without exception.

explanation: Evidence-Based Practice combines rigorous research evidence, clinical expertise, and patient preferences to guide safe and effective care. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h7)

question: Why is critical appraisal of scientific literature important when assessing complementary therapies?

options.A: It helps nurses distinguish between scientifically validated therapies and unproven or harmful practices.
options.B: It guarantees that all herbal products will become free of charge.
options.C: It proves that traditional healing has no place in modern society.
options.D: It allows nurses to write medical prescriptions without a physician.

explanation: Critical appraisal helps clinicians evaluate research methodology and evidence quality, ensuring safe distinction between helpful and unproven CAM modalities. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h7)
